items.q: Why do supersets rank so high?
items.a: Pairing **non-competing exercises** saves a lot of time for **nearly the same results**.

items.q: How do you know you rested enough between superset rounds?
items.a: You can **match your performance** on the first exercise when you come back to it.

items.q: How long should a training block last?
items.a: About **4-10 weeks** with one focus; a block **under 4 weeks** usually means bad programming or no patience.
Only when **performance says so**, and it can be **3 days** instead of a fixed week.
Spreading volume over **more sessions**, like 2-3 sets four times a week instead of 5 sets twice.

items.q: Why does spreading sets help strength?
items.a: Fatigue isn't linear: **later sets cost far more**, so fresher sets mean **higher-quality work**.

items.q: When does a power set stop building power?
items.a: The moment you **lose speed** in the set.
**Submaximal sets** of one movement **spread through the day**, far from failure.

items.q: What did Keith Baar find about tendons?
items.a: They respond to about **10 minutes** of loading, then not again for roughly **6 hours**.

items.q: What's the warning sign when greasing the groove?
items.a: **Aches near where a muscle attaches to a joint**: back off right away.
For **short sessions or maintaining** on holiday, not for heavy strength skills.

items.q: What are cluster sets good for?
items.a: Breaking through a **plateau** on technical lifts with **short ~30 s rests** inside a set.

items.q: Why do circuits and HIIT rank low for strength?
items.a: **Technique slips** with fatigue and **progressive overload** gets lost.

items.q: Which split fits 3-4 training days a week?
items.a: **Full body**; save push/pull splits for **5-7 days** a week.
